sections.label: Support for the everyday challenges that matter most
text: Support for the everyday challenges that matter most
We work with children and young people from age 2 to 18, alongside the adults who support them.
Fine & Gross Motor Skills
Handwriting difficulties, scissor skills, dressing, balance, and coordination challenges affecting daily tasks.
Sensory Processing
Over- or under-sensitivity to touch, sound, movement or textures that make everyday environments overwhelming.
Attention & Self-Regulation
Support for children with ADHD, anxiety, or emotional regulation difficulties that impact focus and behaviour.
Autism & Neurodivergence
Individualised, strengths-based therapy for autistic children and those with other neurodevelopmental profiles.
Daily Living Skills
Building independence with feeding, dressing, toileting, sleep routines and self-care.
School Readiness & Access
Assessments and strategies to help children participate fully in the classroom and playground.
Who We Help

sections.label: Assessment and therapy, tailored to each child
text: Assessment and therapy, tailored to each child
Every plan starts with understanding — then moves into practical, measurable support.
🔍 Comprehensive OT Assessment

A thorough, standardised assessment of your child's sensory processing, motor skills and daily functioning, resulting in a clear, actionable report — including reports suitable for EHCP applications and tribunals.
🌱 Individual Therapy Programmes
Regular one-to-one sessions in clinic, at home, or at school, using a play-based and evidence-informed approach to build skills that transfer into everyday life.
👨‍👩‍👧 Parent & Carer Coaching
Guided strategies and coaching sessions for parents and carers, so progress continues well beyond the therapy room.
🏫 School Consultation & Training
Classroom observations, environment audits, and staff training to help schools implement practical, sustainable adjustments.
🎧 Sensory Diets & Equipment Guidance
Personalised sensory diets and advice on equipment — from weighted blankets to seating — matched to your child's specific needs.
🤝 Small Group Programmes
Social, motor and self-regulation groups that let children practise new skills alongside peers in a supportive setting.
What We Offer

sections.label: A simple, transparent path to support
text: A simple, transparent path to support
Free Discovery Call
A no-obligation 15-minute call to talk through your concerns and see if we're the right fit.
Assessment
A detailed assessment in clinic, at home or at school, using standardised tools and observation.
Personalised Plan
A written report with clear goals and recommendations, shared with you and, where relevant, the school.
Ongoing Therapy
Regular sessions with progress reviews, adapting the plan as your child develops.
How It Works

sections.label: Therapy that fits into real family life, not the other way r
text: Therapy that fits into real family life, not the other way round
Sensphere was founded on a simple belief: children make the most progress when therapy happens in the places and routines that matter to them — not in isolation from home and school.

Our team of qualified, HCPC-registered occupational therapists works collaboratively with parents, carers, teachers and other professionals, so every recommendation is realistic, specific, and actually gets used.
Child-led, play-based sessions grounded in evidence
Close collaboration with schools, SENCOs and GPs
Clear, jargon-free reports you can actually use
Flexible delivery: in clinic, at home, or in school

sections.label: Frequently asked questions
text: Frequently asked questions
Do I need a referral from a GP or paediatrician?
No — you can self-refer directly to Sensphere. Many of our families come to us without a formal referral, though we're happy to work alongside any professionals already involved.
Where do sessions take place?
We offer assessments and therapy at our clinic, in your home, or at your child's school, depending on what suits your family and your child's goals best.
Can your reports be used for an EHCP or tribunal?
Yes. Our assessment reports are written to a standard suitable for EHCP needs assessments, annual reviews, and tribunal evidence, and our therapists have experience giving evidence when required.
How long is the waiting list?
Waiting times vary by location and service, but we aim to offer an initial consultation within two to three weeks. Get in touch and we'll give you the most current estimate.
Do you accept funding through Direct Payments or Personal Budgets?
Yes, we regularly work with families using Direct Payments, Personal Health Budgets, and Local Authority funding. Get in touch and we'll talk you through what's needed.
What areas of the UK do you cover?

Our therapists visit families and schools across England, with clinic bases in several major cities. We also offer selected assessments and consultations remotely — ask us about availability in your area.
